name: Tyler Technologies
description: Tyler sells software to state and local governments: back-office systems for administration, courts and public safety, schools, and property records, plus payment processing and digital services for the public. Subscriptions are 68 percent of revenue, split between SaaS fees ($778M) and transaction-based fees ($808M) that Tyler earns when citizens pay government bills, fines and fees online; maintenance on older on-premises licences is another 19 percent. Customers are public-sector agencies on multi-year contracts that are mostly recurring, and it has not paid a dividend since entering software in 1998. Revenue grew 9 percent in 2025 as clients moved from on-premises licences to SaaS.

Mowgli classification is not set here.

employees.note: Approximately 7,800 team members; about 93% work in the US (FY2025 10-K)

businessLines.name: Enterprise Software (ES)
businessLines.how: Government clients pay multi-year SaaS subscriptions (SaaS $691M in 2025), residual maintenance on on-premises licences ($423M, shrinking as clients convert) and one-time implementation services ($214M); some usage-based transaction fees ($318M).
businessLines.description: Software systems and services for mission-critical government back-office functions: public administration, courts and public safety, education, and property and recording.

revenue.note: FY2024 segment figures in the 10-K; ES operating income +21% in 2025 on $215M more subscription revenue. Share is of consolidated revenue $2,332.3M (segments total $2,323.0M)

businessLines.revenueNote: FY2024 segment figures in the 10-K; ES operating income +21% in 2025 on $215M more subscription revenue. Share is of consolidated revenue $2,332.3M (segments total $2,323.0M)

businessLines.name: Platform Technologies (PT)
businessLines.how: Mostly transaction-based fees earned when constituents pay governments online (payment processing, $490.3M, 78% of the segment); smaller SaaS ($86.5M) and services. Revenue scales with payment volume, with merchant fees as a cost.
businessLines.description: Platform and transformative solutions for public entities: digital solutions, payment processing, streamlined data processing and improved workflows.

revenue.note: Segment operating income fell 9% in 2025 on about $10.7M of loss reserves for two state contracts and higher merchant fees. Share is of consolidated revenue
